what_its_for: Hydrocortisone butyrate is a mild-to-medium strength steroid cream, ointment, or lotion used to treat skin conditions that cause redness, itching, swelling, and irritation. These include eczema (atopic dermatitis), psoriasis, allergic skin reactions, and other inflammatory skin conditions. It works by calming down the immune response in the skin to reduce inflammation and discomfort.
how_to_take: This medicine is for use on the skin only — never swallow it or put it near your eyes, mouth, or inside your nose. Before applying, gently wash and dry the affected area. Apply a thin layer of the cream, ointment, or lotion to the affected skin and gently rub it in. Wash your hands before and after applying, unless your hands are the area being treated. Do not cover the treated area with bandages or tight wrappings unless your doctor tells you to, as this can increase the amount of medicine absorbed into your body. Do not use it on broken, infected, or open skin unless directed by your doctor.
dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected area 2 to 3 times daily, or as directed by your doctor. Use only the smallest amount needed to control your symptoms. Do not use it more often than prescribed. Your doctor will tell you how long to use this medicine — most people use it for only a short period of time (usually no more than 2 to 4 weeks) to avoid side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra medicine to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tube or bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine away from heat and direct sunlight. Do not freeze the lotion or cream. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist how to do this.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, mouth, or on any mucous membranes. Do not use this medicine on your face, groin, or underarms unless your doctor specifically tells you to, as these areas absorb more medicine and are at higher risk for side effects. Avoid using large amounts over large areas of skin for long periods of time. Do not use other skin products, cosmetics, or moisturizers on the same area at the same time without checking with your doctor. Avoid tight clothing or bandages over the treated area unless instructed. Do not use it on a child's diaper area, as diapers act like a bandage and increase absorption.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: skin infections (redness, warmth, pus, or increased pain), skin thinning, stretch marks, or easy bruising in the treated area, acne or unusual hair growth on the skin, your skin condition is getting worse instead of better, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, unusual weight gain, swelling, or extreme tiredness (which could be signs of too much steroid being absorbed into your body), or if your child has slow growth or weight changes.
when_it_works: Most people start to notice improvement in itching and redness within a few days of starting treatment. Full improvement may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use. If your symptoms do not improve after 2 weeks, contact your doctor. This medicine controls symptoms but does not cure the underlying skin condition — your symptoms may return after stopping the medicine.
special_populations: Children: Use with extra caution in children, especially infants. Children absorb more medicine through the skin and are more likely to have side effects. Use only as directed by a pediatrician, for the shortest time possible, and avoid the diaper area. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine. Use only if clearly needed, in small amounts, for the shortest time possible. If breastfeeding, avoid applying to the chest or breast area to prevent your baby from coming into contact with it. Elderly patients: Older adults may have thinner skin and may be more sensitive to side effects such as skin thinning and bruising. Use with care and follow your doctor's guidance closely.
